label: History
value: The Cowardly Lion first encountered Dorothy in the forest along the yellow brick road.
unit: The Cowardly Lion first encountered Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Toto in the forest along the yellow brick road, where he admitted his cowardice and agreed to join them on their journey to see the Great Oz. Along the way, he carried his companions across a deep chasm, swam across a swift river pulling their raft, and defended them against Kalidahs and Winkies. After falling asleep in a field of deadly scarlet poppies, he was rescued by thousands of field mice harnessed to a wooden truck. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he faced Oz in the form of a glowing Ball of Fire and was instructed to help slay the Wicked Witch of the West. During their journey to the West, he was captured by Winged Monkeys and imprisoned in a iron-fenced yard by the Witch, who attempted to starve him into submission, though Dorothy secretly fed him every night. Following the Witch's destruction, he returned to the Emerald City, where Oz gave him a liquid draught from a green-gold dish, which granted him full confidence in his courage. Later, while traveling to the Land of the South to help Dorothy find Glinda, he slew a monstrous giant spider that had been terrorizing a grand old forest, whereupon the forest animals proclaimed him their King. Glinda subsequently commanded the Winged Monkeys to carry him back to his forest domain after Dorothy returned to Kansas.

label: History
value: Dorothy lived in a small one-room house in Kansas
unit: Dorothy lived in a small one-room house in Kansas with her Aunt Em and Uncle Henry until a violent cyclone lifted the house into the air. The house landed in the Land of Oz directly on the Wicked Witch of the East, freeing the Munchkins. Advised by the Witch of the North, Dorothy put on the deceased witch's silver shoes and set off along the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City to ask the Wizard Oz for help returning home. Along the way, she befriended the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, each seeking a gift from Oz. Upon reaching the Emerald City, Oz demanded that they kill the Wicked Witch of the West before granting their wishes. Dorothy defeated the Wicked Witch by throwing a bucket of water on her, causing her to melt. Returning to the Emerald City, the group discovered Oz was a human trickster, and after he departed in a hot-air balloon without her, Dorothy journeyed South to consult Glinda the Good Witch. Glinda revealed that the magic silver shoes could transport her anywhere instantly, enabling Dorothy to return safely to Kansas with Toto.

Advised by the Witch of the North, Dorothy put on the deceased witch's silver shoes and set off along the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City to ask the Wizard Oz for help returning home. Along the way, she befriended the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, each seeking a gift from Oz. Upon reaching the Emerald City, Oz demanded that they kill the Wicked Witch of the West before granting their wishes. Dorothy defeated the Wicked Witch by throwing a bucket of water on her, causing her to melt. Returning to the Emerald City, the group discovered Oz was a human trickster, and after he departed in a hot-air balloon without her, Dorothy journeyed South to consult Glinda the Good Witch. Glinda revealed that the magic silver shoes could transport her anywhere instantly, enabling Dorothy to return safely to Kansas with Toto.

value: Glinda is gentle.
unit: Glinda is gentle, kind, and gracious to everyone who seeks her help. Although sweet and serene, she is also obstinate, firm, and uncompromising when dealing with falsehoods or wicked deeds. She prefers honesty and avoids using deceptive transformations or unnecessary cruelty.

label: History
value: Glinda instructed Dorothy on how to use the Silver Shoes to return to Kansas.
unit: When Dorothy Gale and her companions reached Glinda's castle, Glinda instructed Dorothy on how to use the Silver Shoes to return to Kansas and obtained the Golden Cap, using its remaining commands to transport Dorothy's companions safely to their desired destinations. Later, when the Scarecrow and his allies fled the usurpation of General Jinjur, they traveled to Glinda's castle to request aid. Glinda consulted her records and deduced that Mombi had assisted the Wizard in hiding Princess Ozma, the rightful heir to the Emerald City. Glinda marched her highly disciplined army of girl soldiers to the Emerald City to capture Mombi. After uncovering Mombi's shapeshifting trickery, Glinda pursued the witch across the desert on the Saw-Horse, capturing her with a magical golden thread. She then forced Mombi under threat of punishment to reveal that the boy Tip was in fact the enchanted Princess Ozma. Following Tip's restoration to her true form as Ozma, Glinda flew aboard the Gump into the royal courtyard, captured Jinjur, and successfully restored Princess Ozma to the throne.

label: History
value: Jack was constructed out of wood by Tip.
unit: Jack was constructed out of wood and a carved pumpkin by Tip in order to scare Mombi. Mombi used her newly acquired Powder of Life on him, bringing him to life. After Mombi locked him in a stable, Tip rescued him and they fled together toward the Emerald City. Along the way, Tip brought a Saw-Horse to life so Jack could ride it and spare his joints. The Saw-Horse ran away with Jack, carrying him ahead to the Emerald City, where he was presented to the Scarecrow and became his friend. When General Jinjur's army captured the city, Jack escaped with Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Saw-Horse on their way to seek help from the Tin Woodman. After having his head retrieved from a river and getting a replacement leg made from a table leg by the Tin Woodman, Jack joined the group on their journey to Glinda's territory and their subsequent recapture of the Emerald City. He remained in the Emerald City with Ozma for the rest of his days.

unit: Jack was constructed out of wood and a carved pumpkin by Tip in order to scare Mombi. Mombi used her newly acquired Powder of Life on him, bringing him to life. After Mombi locked him in a stable, Tip rescued him and they fled together toward the Emerald City. Along the way, Tip brought a Saw-Horse to life so Jack could ride it and spare his joints. The Saw-Horse ran away with Jack, carrying him ahead to the Emerald City, where he was presented to the Scarecrow and became his friend. When General Jinjur's army captured the city, Jack escaped with Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Saw-Horse on their way to seek help from the Tin Woodman. After having his head retrieved from a river and getting a replacement leg made from a table leg by the Tin Woodman, Jack joined the group on their journey to Glinda's territory and their subsequent recapture of the Emerald City. He remained in the Emerald City with Ozma for the rest of his days.

label: History
value: General Jinjur secretly assembled the Army of Revolt.
unit: General Jinjur secretly assembled the Army of Revolt, a force composed entirely of young women from all four regions of Oz armed with knitting-needles. She marched her troops to the Emerald City, easily intimidated the Guardian of the Gate, and seized power from the Scarecrow without shedding blood. After declaring herself Queen, she occupied the palace and ordered her followers to pry the precious emeralds from the city walls and streets. Fearing a counter-attack by the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, she allied with the witch Mombi. When Glinda the Good marched upon the city to demand Mombi and restore the rightful ruler, Jinjur attempted to stall using flags of truce and deceptive tricks devised by the witch. After Glinda's forces breached the palace using the Gump, Jinjur was captured in the courtyard, chained, and deposed. Upon her surrender, the rebellion collapsed, her army was disbanded, and Jinjur was released after promising good behavior.

label: History
value: Mombi lived in the Gillikin Country
unit: Mombi lived in the Gillikin Country where she raised Tip and practiced forbidden magic as a sorceress. After trading magic secrets with a crooked mountain wizard, she returned home and tested the Powder of Life on a pumpkin-headed dummy Tip made, bringing it to life. Angry at Tip's trickery, she attempted to brew a potion to turn him into a marble statue, but Tip escaped with the live dummy and her Powder of Life. Later, Mombi was summoned by General Jinjur to assist the Army of Revolt in stopping the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and she conjured illusions to impede their travels. When Glinda marched on the Emerald City to capture Mombi and find Princess Ozma, Mombi repeatedly used magical transformations to disguise herself and evade capture, taking the forms of Jellia Jamb, a red rose, a shadow, an ant, and a griffin. Glinda pursued and captured her in the desert using a magical golden thread. Brought back to camp, Mombi attempted to lie, but Glinda's magic truth-reading pearl exposed her false statements. Threatened with death, Mombi confessed that the Wizard had brought her the infant Ozma, whom she transformed into Tip. Under Glinda's orders, Mombi performed a final spell that restored Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma.

When Glinda marched on the Emerald City to capture Mombi and find Princess Ozma, Mombi repeatedly used magical transformations to disguise herself and evade capture, taking the forms of Jellia Jamb, a red rose, a shadow, an ant, and a griffin. Glinda pursued and captured her in the desert using a magical golden thread. Brought back to camp, Mombi attempted to lie, but Glinda's magic truth-reading pearl exposed her false statements. Threatened with death, Mombi confessed that the Wizard had brought her the infant Ozma, whom she transformed into Tip. Under Glinda's orders, Mombi performed a final spell that restored Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma.

label: History
value: The Wizard of Oz usurped the throne of the Emerald City.
unit: When the Wizard of Oz usurped the throne of the Emerald City, he took the baby Ozma and concealed her with the witch Mombi. Mombi enchanted the child into a boy named Tip and raised him, keeping her true identity secret for years. Glinda the Good eventually captured Mombi and forced her to reveal Ozma's whereabouts, uncovering that Tip was the enchanted princess. Mombi restored Ozma to her rightful form, after which Glinda led an army to reclaim the Emerald City from Queen Jinjur. Following Jinjur's surrender, Ozma ascended the throne as Queen, ordered the restoration of stolen jewels, disbanded the Army of Revolt, and granted the Gump's wish to be disassembled. She took care of her personal mount, the Saw-Horse, capping its wooden legs with gold, and established a wise and peaceful rule with the assistance of Glinda and the Woggle-Bug.

label: Appearance
value: The Saw-Horse is constructed from an animated log body.
unit: The Saw-Horse is constructed from an animated log body with a branch sticking up like a tail, two eye-like knots, and a chopped-out mouth. Its four legs were originally straight tree branches spread wide apart, lacking knee-joints, causing it to rock side to side when walking. Its ears are whittled out of tree bark and inserted into bored holes, and a post was hammered into its back to give riders something to hold onto. Later, its broken left leg was replaced using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden legs, and its wooden legs were eventually shod with gold.

label: History
value: Tip brought the wooden saw-horse to life with the Powder of Life.
unit: After Tip brought the wooden saw-horse to life with the Powder of Life, he carved bark ears and drove a wooden post into its back so it could hear commands and carry Jack Pumpkinhead. The Saw-Horse carried Jack on the journey to the Emerald City, swimming across a river and galloping ahead so fast that Tip was accidentally left behind. At the Emerald City, it was locked in the royal treasury by the Scarecrow's soldier, who treated it as a jewel and fed it sawdust. During the rebellion led by General Jinjur, the Saw-Horse carried Tip, the Scarecrow, and Jack Pumpkinhead in a daring escape from the palace, leaping into a river to float them to safety. On the journey to consult the Tin Woodman, the Saw-Horse broke one of its legs in a rabbit hole, which was subsequently replaced with a modified wooden leg taken from Jack Pumpkinhead. Later, during the pursuit of old Mombi, Glinda mounted the Saw-Horse to chase down the Witch transformed as a Griffin, wearing the creature down across the desert due to its untiring wooden limbs. Following Tip's transformation into Queen Ozma, the Saw-Horse became her personal property and mount, receiving golden shoes on its legs to prevent them from wearing out.

During the rebellion led by General Jinjur, the Saw-Horse carried Tip, the Scarecrow, and Jack Pumpkinhead in a daring escape from the palace, leaping into a river to float them to safety. On the journey to consult the Tin Woodman, the Saw-Horse broke one of its legs in a rabbit hole, which was subsequently replaced with a modified wooden leg taken from Jack Pumpkinhead. Later, during the pursuit of old Mombi, Glinda mounted the Saw-Horse to chase down the Witch transformed as a Griffin, wearing the creature down across the desert due to its untiring wooden limbs. Following Tip's transformation into Queen Ozma, the Saw-Horse became her personal property and mount, receiving golden shoes on its legs to prevent them from wearing out.

label: Appearance
value: The Scarecrow's head is a small sack.

He wears an old blue pointed Munchkin hat—later replaced by a heavy golden crown set with jewels while king—along with blue-topped boots and cotton-padded gloves. After losing his straw stuffing to Jackdaws, his clothes and boots are stuffed entirely with paper money.

value: The Scarecrow is cheerful.
unit: The Scarecrow is cheerful, polite, and unselfishly devoted to his friends, remaining calm and thoughtful even under dire circumstances. Despite insisting he has no brains, he frequently comes up with practical ideas and values wisdom far above physical comfort or wealth.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow was rescued from a pole in a Munchkin cornfield by Dorothy.
unit: Rescued from a pole in a Munchkin cornfield by Dorothy, the Scarecrow joined her on a journey to the Emerald City to ask the Great Oz for brains. Along the way, he helped defeat crows, Kalidahs, and the Wicked Witch of the West. Upon returning to the Emerald City, Oz gave him a brain made of bran, pins, and needles, and appointed him ruler of the city before leaving in his balloon. Later, General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt overthrew the Scarecrow, forcing him to flee to his friend the Tin Woodman for aid. During their retreat, his straw was stolen by Jackdaws, so his friends stuffed his clothing with paper money. With the help of Glinda the Good Sorceress and Princess Ozma, the Emerald City was restored to its rightful heir, and the Scarecrow stepped down as king to become the Royal Treasurer of the Winkies.

label: Appearance
value: The Tin Woodman is composed entirely of pieces of tin.
unit: The Tin Woodman is composed entirely of pieces of tin, soldered and riveted together into the form of a man, with a body and joints that move on hinges. His tin head works freely when well oiled, and his breast features a patched square where his heart was placed. He is often seen carrying an axe and an oil-can, and later wears a diamond necklace around his neck.

value: The Tin Woodman is exceptionally polite.

He is fiercely loyal to his comrades and willing to fight courageously when they are threatened. He holds a strong belief that a good heart and happiness are the most valuable things in the world.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman was standing completely rusted in the forest holding an axe.
unit: While standing completely rusted in the forest holding an axe, the Tin Woodman was discovered by Dorothy and the Scarecrow, who oiled his joints and freed him. Seeking a heart, he joined Dorothy's party on their journey along the yellow brick road to see the Great Oz in the Emerald City. Along the way, he cleared paths, built a raft, saved a field mouse queen, and defended the group against forty wolves sent by the Wicked Witch of the West. Though dropped onto sharp rocks and battered by the Winged Monkeys, he was repaired by the tinsmiths of the Winkies and later received a silk-and-sawdust heart from Oz. After helping Dorothy, he accepted the invitation of the Winkies to become their Emperor. When the dethroned Scarecrow fled to his castle for assistance, the Tin Woodman joined him to help reclaim the Emerald City. He constructed the Flying Gump out of miscellaneous palace items, fought off Jackdaws, and ultimately accompanied the group to Glinda's realm, where he agreed to welcome the Scarecrow as his Royal Treasurer and continue ruling the Winkies.

Along the way, he cleared paths, built a raft, saved a field mouse queen, and defended the group against forty wolves sent by the Wicked Witch of the West. Though dropped onto sharp rocks and battered by the Winged Monkeys, he was repaired by the tinsmiths of the Winkies and later received a silk-and-sawdust heart from Oz. After helping Dorothy, he accepted the invitation of the Winkies to become their Emperor. When the dethroned Scarecrow fled to his castle for assistance, the Tin Woodman joined him to help reclaim the Emerald City. He constructed the Flying Gump out of miscellaneous palace items, fought off Jackdaws, and ultimately accompanied the group to Glinda's realm, where he agreed to welcome the Scarecrow as his Royal Treasurer and continue ruling the Winkies.

label: Personality
value: Tip is a mischievous boy.
unit: Tip is a mischievous and energetic boy who loves playing tricks and testing his handiwork. He frankly shows his dislikes and hates being mistreated or forced into hard labor, taking care not to exhaust his strength. He is resourceful and practical in dangerous situations, yet shows genuine concern and loyalty for the wooden creations he brings to life. Though reluctant about unwanted responsibilities or changes, he demonstrates courage and adaptability.

label: History
value: Tip was raised in the Country of the Gillikins.
unit: Tip was raised in the Country of the Gillikins by the old sorceress Mombi, who made him perform farm labor. To prank Mombi, Tip constructed a wooden man with a carved pumpkin head named Jack Pumpkinhead. After Mombi brought Jack to life using the Powder of Life and threatened to transform Tip into a marble statue, Tip fled with Jack and stolen magic powder. On their journey toward the Emerald City, Tip used the powder to bring a wooden Saw-Horse to life. Upon learning that General Jinjur's Army of Revolt was invading the Emerald City, Tip joined the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and their companions. He helped construct and animate a flying creature called the Gump to escape the trapped palace. After various adventures, the group sought assistance from Glinda the Good. Glinda forced Mombi to confess that Tip was originally Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz whom Mombi had transformed into a boy as an infant. Tip reluctantly agreed to be restored to his true form, becoming Princess Ozma once more.

label: History
value: Toto lived with Dorothy.
unit: Toto lived with Dorothy on a small farm in Kansas, where his playful nature kept Dorothy laughing and happy. When a cyclone carried their house away to the Land of Oz, Toto was transported alongside Dorothy. He accompanied Dorothy on her journey down the yellow brick road to the Emerald City, meeting the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. During their travels, Toto bravely rushed at a roaring Lion to protect Dorothy, chased field mice, and survived dangerous encounters with the Kalidahs and the deadly poppy field. Upon reaching the Wicked Witch of the West's territory, Toto was captured alongside Dorothy by Winged Monkeys, and he even bit the Wicked Witch when she hit him with her umbrella. After the Witch was melted and Oz departed in his balloon, Toto accompanied the party to Glinda's castle in the South. When Glinda instructed Dorothy on how to use the Silver Shoes, Dorothy picked up Toto and they were magically transported back to their Kansas farm.

label: History
value: The Wizard was born in Omaha.
unit: Born in Omaha, the Wizard worked as a trained ventriloquist and later as a balloonist. When his balloon drifted into the Land of Oz, the local inhabitants mistook him for a powerful magician. He usurped the throne from King Pastoria and entrusted Pastoria's baby daughter, Ozma, to the witch Mombi to be hidden away. He ordered the construction of the Emerald City and mandated that everyone wear green spectacles. Fearing discovery, he isolated himself in his palace and used elaborate illusions and ventriloquism to appear to visitors as a giant head, a lovely lady, a monster, or a ball of fire. When Dorothy Gale and her companions arrived demanding favors, he required them to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West first. Upon their successful return, Toto accidentally knocked over a screen, exposing him as an ordinary old man. He fulfilled his guests' desires through clever trickery and constructed a green silk hot-air balloon to escape back to his homeland, accidentally leaving Dorothy behind when the balloon prematurely broke its ropes and floated away into the sky.

label: Appearance
value: The Woggle-Bug is a highly magnified bug.
unit: The Woggle-Bug is a highly magnified, dark-brown bug with a flat body striped in light brown and white in the front, supported on two slender legs with curled toes. He has slender arms, a long neck, and a humanlike head with bulging black eyes, a nose ending in a curling feeler, and ears with antennae resembling pig tails. Fully as tall as the Tin Woodman, he wears a dark-blue swallowtail coat with yellow silk lining, a flower in the buttonhole, a tight white duck vest, fawn-colored plush knickerbockers with gilt buckles, a tall silk hat, and two wrought gold bracelets on his slender arms.

label: History
value: The Woggle-Bug grew up as an ordinary insect in Oz
unit: The Woggle-Bug grew up as an ordinary insect in Oz before making his home in a hearth crack inside Professor Nowitall's schoolhouse, where he spent three years absorbing lectures and gaining a vast education. One day, Professor Nowitall caught him and projected his image onto a screen using a magnifying glass; during a commotion, the Woggle-Bug escaped while remaining highly magnified. After saving a tailor's ninth life, he was rewarded with a tailored suit of fine clothes. While traveling toward the Emerald City, he encountered Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, joining their company. Along the journey, he frequently showcased his erudition through puns and philosophical comments, though his companions occasionally scolded him for them. After reaching the Emerald City and escaping Queen Jinjur's forces aboard the newly animated Gump, the group crashed into a giant Jackdaw nest, where the Woggle-Bug was saved from the birds by the Scarecrow's sacrifice. He later used one of the Silver Wishing Pills to mend the Gump's wings, allowing the party to fly to Glinda the Good's realm. After Jinjur was defeated and Princess Ozma was restored to the throne, the Woggle-Bug was appointed to the post of Public Educator and tried unsuccessfully to educate Jack Pumpkinhead.

unit: The Woggle-Bug grew up as an ordinary insect in Oz before making his home in a hearth crack inside Professor Nowitall's schoolhouse, where he spent three years absorbing lectures and gaining a vast education. One day, Professor Nowitall caught him and projected his image onto a screen using a magnifying glass; during a commotion, the Woggle-Bug escaped while remaining highly magnified. After saving a tailor's ninth life, he was rewarded with a tailored suit of fine clothes. While traveling toward the Emerald City, he encountered Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, joining their company. Along the journey, he frequently showcased his erudition through puns and philosophical comments, though his companions occasionally scolded him for them. After reaching the Emerald City and escaping Queen Jinjur's forces aboard the newly animated Gump, the group crashed into a giant Jackdaw nest, where the Woggle-Bug was saved from the birds by the Scarecrow's sacrifice. He later used one of the Silver Wishing Pills to mend the Gump's wings, allowing the party to fly to Glinda the Good's realm. After Jinjur was defeated and Princess Ozma was restored to the throne, the Woggle-Bug was appointed to the post of Public Educator and tried unsuccessfully to educate Jack Pumpkinhead.
